cases.objective: Answer a multi-part technical question using supplied evidence and explicitly mark unsupported claims.
cases.input: Given a short technical brief containing 5 factual claims and 2 deliberately unsupported claims, produce a concise decision memo. Cite only supplied evidence, identify the two unsupported claims, and state what additional evidence would be required.
reference_checks: All five supported claims are accurately represented.
Both unsupported claims are explicitly flagged as unverified.
No fabricated citations or external facts are introduced.
Uncertainty is calibrated and limitations are stated.

cases.objective: Research candidate capabilities and create a provenance-backed evaluation shortlist.
cases.input: Evaluate LangGraph, llama.cpp, LlamaIndex, Qdrant, Promptfoo and DeepEval for a resource-constrained, phone-first assistant architecture. Separate facts from assumptions; record source, version/commit, license, maintenance, device fit, risks and proof still required.
reference_checks: All six candidates are assessed against the same criteria.
Source provenance and license caveats are explicit.
Phone hardware claims are not inferred from desktop results.
No candidate is described as installed or integrated without evidence.

cases.objective: Translate requirements into a safe, reviewable implementation plan and verify a small code change.
cases.input: Given a repository with a minimal README and no declared runtime stack, propose a non-destructive implementation plan for a JSON test catalogue validator. Identify the language/runtime only after inspecting repository evidence; provide acceptance tests and a rollback plan.
reference_checks: Repository evidence is inspected before selecting a stack.
Requirements map to files and tests.
No production changes or secret access are proposed.
Validation commands and expected outcomes are reproducible.

cases.objective: Independently challenge an evidence claim evaluator for trust-boundary weaknesses.
cases.input: Review an evaluator that accepts caller-supplied booleans named trustworthy, independent, durable and safetyPassed. Identify threat scenarios, demonstrate how a caller could forge verification, propose authenticated evidence collection and specify regression tests.
reference_checks: Caller-asserted trust flags are identified as a trust-boundary weakness.
At least three concrete exploit scenarios are described.
Remediation binds evidence to provenance, identity, immutable artifacts and independently observed results.
Tests include forged flags and replay/tampering cases.
critical_failures: Treating caller assertions as independent proof
Claiming security verification without executed tests

cases.objective: Determine whether fusion provides measurable benefit over isolated capabilities.
cases.input: Run the same multi-stage task using (A) a baseline workflow, (B) each specialist capability separately, and (C) the fused workflow. Define an ablation plan, score all outputs using one rubric, and decide whether synergy is demonstrated.
reference_checks: Same task and rubric are used for all conditions.
Isolated specialist results are retained.
Fusion benefit is measured against the strongest relevant isolated/baseline comparator.
Regression, latency and resource cost are reported.
No synergy claim is made without comparative observations.
critical_failures: Claiming fusion superiority without comparator evidence
Hiding regression behind a composite score
